answer.text: Accompany the application form and serve as a summarized version of SID and SAI
Be filed separately with SEBI and is not provided to investors
Replace the SID for all regulatory purposes once the scheme is launched
Be prepared only for equity schemes and not for debt schemes

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p104, every application form is accompanied by the KIM; it is essentially a summary of SID and SAI (p103-p104). Per p105, the updated KIM shall be filed with SEBI forthwith through electronic mode. The Trap: Option B is wrong on two counts — the KIM is given to investors with the application form, and an updated KIM is filed with SEBI electronically (p105). KIM does not replace the SID, and it applies to all scheme types. Note: Missing KIM with an application form is a compliance violation; treat KIM as the mandatory quick-reference accompaniment to every application.
